---
task: "Build require-payment, resend-link, abandoned sweep, member cancel link"
slug: 20261010-accessbuddy-require-payment-build
project: accessbuddy
effort: advanced
effort_source: classifier
phase: observe
progress: 0/36
mode: interactive
started: 2026-10-10T09:00:00+11:00
updated: 2026-10-10T09:00:00+11:00
---

## Problem

AccessBuddy has no admin action to demand payment on a request, no way to resend a payment link, and a member who abandons the Stripe step leaves the request in SUBMITTED where no queue column renders it and no reminder targets it. The only email that carries a pay link is the exemption-rejected email. Members have no cancel path from an email.

## Vision

An approver opens any unpaid request and sees "Require payment" or "Resend payment link". The member gets a branded email with a Pay button and a "Cancel this request" link that works without signing in. Overnight, abandoned requests move themselves to Awaiting Payment and the member is emailed. Nothing silently sits in SUBMITTED again.

## Out of Scope

No manual "record offline payment" action. No change to Stripe account model or webhooks beyond intent cancellation hygiene. No migration (the cancel link is a signed token, not a stored column). No deploy; this ships as a PR for Nick to merge.

## Constraints

- Branch from origin/main; PR #102 branch untouched.
- Postgres RLS: writes go through withTenant; cron selects follow the existing bare-db pattern.
- Email rendering goes through sendTemplatedEmail so setEmailBranding runs.
- No new env vars; cancel token signs with the existing SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET.
- bun only; TypeScript only; Australian English in copy.
- Commit prefix feat: so release-please ships it on merge.

## Goal

A PR on branch feat/require-payment-and-abandoned-sweep that adds the PAYMENT_REQUIRED transition with intent creation and email, an admin resend-payment-link action, a nightly abandoned-payment sweep, and a signed cancel link on the pay page, with typecheck and tests green.

## Criteria

- [ ] ISC-1: state-machine.ts allows PAYMENT_REQUIRED from AWAITING_APPROVAL as well as SUBMITTED
- [ ] ISC-2: requests.ts resolveNewStatus maps PAYMENT_REQUIRED from AWAITING_APPROVAL to AWAITING_PAYMENT
- [ ] ISC-3: shared state-machine test covers PAYMENT_REQUIRED from both states and rejects it from AWAITING_PROGRAMMING
- [ ] ISC-4: transitionRequest creates a Stripe intent on PAYMENT_REQUIRED when none exists
- [ ] ISC-5: transitionRequest persists paymentAmountCents and paymentExempt=false on PAYMENT_REQUIRED
- [ ] ISC-6: transitionRequest sends the paymentRequired email on PAYMENT_REQUIRED with pay and cancel links
- [ ] ISC-7: new route requests/[id]/payment-required exists, POST, permission APPROVE_EXEMPTION, body {reason}
- [ ] ISC-8: payment-required route refuses paid requests and orphaned requests with a 400
- [ ] ISC-9: new route requests/[id]/resend-payment-link exists, POST, permission APPROVE_EXEMPTION
- [ ] ISC-10: resend route accepts SUBMITTED and AWAITING_PAYMENT only, refuses when paidAt set
- [ ] ISC-11: resend route ensures an intent exists before emailing
- [ ] ISC-12: resend route writes an audit UPDATE entry with metadata.action payment_link_resent
- [ ] ISC-13: shared helper builds paymentUrl and cancelUrl from NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, slug, request id
- [ ] ISC-14: cancel token is HMAC-SHA256 over tenantId, requestId, expiry using SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET
- [ ] ISC-15: cancel token verify rejects tampered signature, wrong request id, and expired token (unit test)
- [ ] ISC-16: new public route requests/[id]/cancel-by-token POST {token, reason} transitions CANCEL when valid
- [ ] ISC-17: cancel-by-token refuses paid requests and non-cancellable statuses
- [ ] ISC-18: pay page shows a "Cancel this request" section only when ?cancel=<token> is present
- [ ] ISC-19: pay page cancel posts to cancel-by-token and renders a cancelled confirmation
- [ ] ISC-20: payment-info returns a cancelled flag (no client secret) for cancelled or rejected requests
- [ ] ISC-21: CANCEL on an unpaid request with an intent cancels the Stripe intent best-effort
- [ ] ISC-22: email-events.ts registers payment_required with amount, paymentUrl, cancelUrl variables
- [ ] ISC-23: email-templates.ts paymentRequiredEmail renders amount, Pay button, cancel link
- [ ] ISC-24: email.ts TemplateVariables and renderTemplate include paymentRequired
- [ ] ISC-25: paymentReminder template accepts paymentUrl and cancelUrl and renders both when given
- [ ] ISC-26: cron reminder passes paymentUrl and cancelUrl to paymentReminder
- [ ] ISC-27: cron has an abandoned-payment sweep over SUBMITTED, non-orphaned, paymentExempt=false, unpaid, older than grace
- [ ] ISC-28: sweep transitions each via transitionRequest PAYMENT_REQUIRED with metadata.action abandoned_payment_sweep
- [ ] ISC-29: cron results include abandonedPaymentsSwept counter
- [ ] ISC-30: admin-actions.tsx shows Require Payment (reason form) when PAYMENT_REQUIRED is valid and unpaid
- [ ] ISC-31: admin-actions.tsx shows Resend Payment Link for SUBMITTED or AWAITING_PAYMENT unpaid requests with APPROVE_EXEMPTION
- [ ] ISC-32: queue-filter.tsx renders a Submitted (unpaid) section so same-day abandoned requests are visible
- [ ] ISC-33: audit-trail.tsx labels submitted_awaiting_payment, awaiting_approval_awaiting_payment, payment_link_resent, abandoned sweep, member cancel via link
- [ ] ISC-34: payment-exempt route accepts SUBMITTED as well as AWAITING_PAYMENT
- [ ] ISC-35: bun typecheck and bun test pass across the monorepo
- [ ] ISC-36: Anti: no change to webhook signature handling, Stripe account model, or PR #102 branch

content.content:
1. **Check Stripe before anything that assumes "unpaid".** The sweep, the resend route, payment-required and cancel-by-token all treat `paidAt` null as unpaid. If a webhook is late or failed, the member has paid but `paidAt` is still null. The sweep would then move them to Awaiting Payment and email "please pay", and the cancel link would cancel a paid request with no refund.
   - Retrieve the intent before acting.
   - If its status is `succeeded` or `processing`, skip it and log it for reconciliation.
   - In cancel-by-token, refuse when the intent is `processing` or `succeeded`. Best-effort cancel of the intent doesn't protect money that has already been taken.

2. **The first sweep will email the whole backlog.** At the first 2am run after merge, every old request stuck in SUBMITTED gets a "payment required" email, including ones that are months old.
   - Add a lower bound, e.g. `createdAt > now() - 14 days`.
   - Or ship with a dry-run flag that only logs.
   - Either way, put the expected first-run count in the PR description so Nick knows what will happen.

3. **Keep the token separate from session tokens.** You're reusing `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`, so the signed message needs its own prefix, e.g. `cancel:v1:${tenantId}:${requestId}:${exp}`. Without it, a token signed for one purpose could be accepted for another. Also:
   - `timingSafeEqual` throws if the two buffers differ in length, which a tampered token causes. Check length first and return 400, not 500.
   - The route must check that the token's `tenantId` matches the tenant from the slug or request. Matching the request id alone isn't enough.

**Should fix (small)**

4. **Stripe and email calls inside a DB transaction.** If you create the intent inside `withTenant` and the transaction then rolls back, the intent is left orphaned. Send the email only after commit, never inside the transaction.
   - Pass an idempotency key to `paymentIntents.create`, e.g. `req-${id}-${amount}`, so a double-click can't create two intents.

5. **"Ensure intent exists" has to cover more than a missing intent.** If the existing intent is `canceled`, which is terminal and happens after a cancel, create a new one. If its amount doesn't match `paymentAmountCents` (the price changed), update or replace it.

6. **Sweep robustness.**
   - Wrap each row in its own try/catch so one Stripe error doesn't stop the run.
   - A request whose credential type has no price will throw every night. Log it once and make sure it shows up somewhere.
   - Each `transitionRequest` call needs a proper `withTenant` scope, not the bare db. Your memory notes a latent bare-db RLS risk in cron at the accessbuddy_app cutover, and this adds a second path into it.
   - Check which actor or `userId` the sweep and the public cancel route record. An audit row with a null user can break the FK or the renderer.

7. **Audit labels.** Your memory says a new `metadata.action` needs labels in *both* renderers. ISC-33 only covers `audit-trail.tsx`. Find the other renderer and add the five new labels there too.

8. **Token in the URL.** The pay page loads Stripe.js, so the `?cancel=` token can leak in the Referer header and in analytics. Set `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` on that page, or remove the parameter with `history.replaceState` after reading it. Cap the length of `reason`.

**Test coverage**

Most route ISCs are checked by reading the code, not by tests. At minimum, add unit tests for:
- the sweep's where-clause
- cancel-by-token refusing paid requests and wrong-tenant tokens

ISC-36 should still record the PR #102 branch sha before and after.

The rest is fine and the decisions hold up: `APPROVE_EXEMPTION` for both actions, the 1-hour grace plus the queue section for same-day requests, idempotent cancel, and no migration. Note in the PR description that PAYMENT_REQUIRED from AWAITING_APPROVAL can override an exemption that was already granted.

cd ~/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/code && git add -A && git commit -q -m "fix(payments): review follow-ups for require-payment flow

- refuse resend / exemption on orphaned requests (link to a member first);
  hide Require Payment and Resend on orphans in the admin UI
- before CANCEL, REJECT, PAYMENT_EXEMPT or APPROVE_EXEMPTION with a live
  intent, ask Stripe: processing blocks the transition, succeeded records
  paidAt so cancel/reject auto-refund, otherwise the intent is voided
- payment-info only hands out a client secret in submitted or
  awaiting_payment so an old emailed link cannot charge after exemption
- sweep no longer requires requesterId: first-time applicants without an
  account (isOrphaned=false, orphanEmail set) are the main case
- void a superseded intent when replacing it for a price change" && git push -q origin feat/require-payment-and-abandoned-sweep 2>&1 | tail -2; git log --oneline -4
cat > /tmp/pr-body.md <<'EOF'
## Why

Today a request only ever reaches **Awaiting Payment** automatically (exemption rejected, or orphan linked). A member who submits a priced request and closes the browser at the Stripe step leaves the request in **SUBMITTED**, where no queue column renders it and no reminder targets it. There was no admin way to demand payment, no way to resend a payment link, and the reminder email had no link in it. Members had no way to cancel from an email without signing in.

## What

**Admin actions** (both behind `approve_exemption`, like Grant Exemption)
- **Require Payment** (`POST requests/[id]/payment-required`, reason required). Valid from SUBMITTED and AWAITING_APPROVAL. Creates the Stripe PaymentIntent if the request never got one, records the amount, moves to AWAITING_PAYMENT and emails the member a pay link plus a cancel link. Rolls back if the credential type has no price. Note: from AWAITING_APPROVAL this can override an exemption that was already granted.
- **Resend Payment Link** (`POST requests/[id]/resend-payment-link`). No status change; re-emails pay + cancel links for SUBMITTED / AWAITING_PAYMENT unpaid requests. Audited as `payment_link_resent`.

**Nightly abandoned-payment sweep** (in the existing daily cron)
- SUBMITTED, not orphaned, not exempt, priced, unpaid, older than 1 hour and younger than 30 days → `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` via the normal transition, so the member gets the payment email. Counter `abandonedPaymentsSwept` in the cron result. The 30 day bound stops the first run emailing a stale backlog; older ones show in the new **Submitted (unpaid)** queue section for manual action.
- Payment reminder email (3+ days) now carries the pay button and cancel link.

**Member cancel from email** (no sign-in)
- The cancel link is `/t/<slug>/pay/<id>?cancel=<token>` where the token is HMAC-SHA256 over `cancel:v1:tenantId:requestId:expiry` keyed with `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`, 30 day TTL, timing-safe compare. No migration, no new secret. Rotating the session secret invalidates outstanding cancel links.
- `POST requests/[id]/cancel-by-token` cancels from SUBMITTED / AWAITING_PAYMENT / AWAITING_EXEMPTION_REVIEW, idempotent, and refuses if Stripe shows a payment succeeded or processing (even when `paidAt` is still null because the webhook is late).
- The pay page shows a "Cancel this request" form only when the token is present, strips the token from the address bar after reading it, and shows a cancelled card afterwards.

**Stripe hygiene**
- Leaving the money-owed states (cancel, reject, exemption granted) with a live intent: ask Stripe first. `processing` blocks the transition; `succeeded` records `paidAt` so cancel/reject auto-refund as before; otherwise the intent is voided so an old emailed link cannot charge.
- `payment-info` only hands out a client secret in SUBMITTED / AWAITING_PAYMENT and reports cancelled / rejected explicitly.
- A cancelled intent (cancel then reopen) or a price change gets a fresh intent; the superseded one is voided.

**Also**
- `payment-exempt` now accepts SUBMITTED (the UI already offered the button; the route rejected it). Orphans refused.
- New `payment_required` email event + code template; audit-trail labels for the new transitions and actions; `docs/FLOWS.md` transition table updated.

## Tests
- shared: PAYMENT_REQUIRED validity per state, require-then-pay and require-then-cancel paths
- web: cancel token sign/verify (tamper, wrong request, wrong tenant, expiry, malformed), link builder, email templates, event registry
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`, `bun run lint` green (lint warnings are pre-existing, untouched files)

## Not in scope
Offline "record cash payment" action; rate limiting on the public cancel route beyond the signed token.

## Review
Advisor pass and an independent code-review agent pass were run; their findings (late-webhook guard, orphan guards, exemption-after-link, sweep requester filter, superseded intents, token in URL) are folded into the last two commits.
EOF

━━━ ✅ VERIFY ━━━ 6/7

✅ VERIFICATION: 36/36 ISCs passed. Local: typecheck 5/5 tasks, tests shared 19 / db 16 / web 193 green, lint 0 errors. CI on PR #104: Build, Lint & Type Check, Test (including the database-gated suites I cannot run here), and Claude Code Review all pass. 📦 DELIVERABLE COMPLIANCE:
 📦 D1 "require payment action": ✓ route, transition, intent creation, email, admin button
 📦 D2 "resend link action": ✓ route, audited, admin button, orphan-guarded
 📦 D3 "sweep ... send a payment link to submitted requests": ✓ nightly cron step, bounded 1h to 30d
 📦 D4 "avenue for them to then cancel": ✓ signed no-sign-in cancel link on the pay page, in every payment email

🔄 RE-READ:
 🔄 "Build the require payment and resend link actions": ✓
 🔄 "create a sweep that will send a payment link to submitted requests if they do leave it": ✓
 🔄 "Ensuring there is an avenue for them to then cancel the request if needed": ✓

━━━ 📚 LEARN ━━━ 7/7

🧠 LEARNING: The one thing I would do differently is check Stripe's intent state from the first draft rather than trusting `paidAt`; both the advisor and the reviewer independently flagged the late-webhook window, which says the gap was obvious from outside. The reviewer also caught that the sweep's requester filter excluded first-time applicants, the main group it exists for, which came from reading the service layer before the production submit route.

🗂️ LEARNING INVENTORY:
 🗂️ paidAt is a cache; Stripe is truth for money moved | TYPE: gotcha | KEEP: yes — written to the ISA Changelog; worth a memory note
 🗂️ Open AccessBuddy PRs via ssh mac gh with body file | TYPE: reference | KEEP: no — already in the prod-access memory

📄 DOC SYNC: SKIP — no PAI system files modified.

━━━ 📃 SUMMARY ━━━ 7/7

🔄 ITERATION on: follow-up to the assessment that found no require-payment action and invisible abandoned SUBMITTED requests.

📃 CONTENT:

**PR #104 is open and green: https://github.com/nicholas-wood/accessbuddy/pull/104** (branch `feat/require-payment-and-abandoned-sweep`, three `feat`/`fix` commits, so release-please ships it on merge). Not merged; that is yours.

**What an admin gets.** On any unpaid request the detail page now shows **Require Payment** (from Submitted or Awaiting Approval, reason required, approver permission) and **Resend Payment Link** (Submitted or Awaiting Payment). Require Payment creates the Stripe intent if the request never had one, records the amount, moves the request to Awaiting Payment and emails the member. Resend emails the same links without changing status and is audited. The queue has a new **Submitted (unpaid)** section so same-day abandoned requests are visible.

**What the sweep does.** The daily 2am cron now moves priced, non-orphaned, unpaid requests that have sat in Submitted for more than an hour (and less than 30 days) to Awaiting Payment through the normal transition, which sends the payment email. The 30 day floor stops the first run emailing a stale backlog; anything older is in the new queue section for a manual decision. The existing 3-day reminder email now carries the pay button and cancel link too.

**What the member gets.** Every payment email has a Pay Now button and a "cancel this request" link. The cancel link opens the same public pay page with a signed token (HMAC over tenant, request and a 30 day expiry, keyed with the existing session secret, so no migration and no new secret). The member gives a reason and cancels without signing in. Cancelling voids the Stripe intent so an old link cannot take money later, and the page then shows a cancelled card.

**Money-safety rules added on the way.** Every action that demands or forgives money asks Stripe for the intent's live state first, because a late webhook leaves `paidAt` null after a real payment. A processing payment blocks cancel, reject and exemption; a succeeded one records payment so cancel and reject auto-refund as before. Granting an exemption now voids the live intent, and the pay page only hands out a client secret while money is actually owed. A cancelled intent (cancel then reopen) or a price change gets a fresh intent.

**Two things to know before merging.** Require Payment from Awaiting Approval can override an exemption that was already granted; that is the intended use but it is a judgement call for the approver. And rotating `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET` invalidates outstanding cancel links in emails (payment links keep working).

**Not built, by design.** No "record cash payment" action, and no rate limiting on the public cancel route beyond the signed token.

🖊️ STORY:
- Abandoned payments vanished and admins could not demand money
- Built require, resend, nightly sweep, signed cancel link
- Two reviews caught late-webhook and orphan money gaps
- PR 104 green; Nick merges when ready

🗣️ Jarvis: PR 104 ships require payment, resend link, abandoned sweep, and email cancel; all checks green.

---
name: gotcha-accessbuddy-paidat-is-a-cache
description: AccessBuddy fobRequests.paidAt lags Stripe; any action that demands or forgives money must read the PaymentIntent from Stripe first
metadata:
  type: project
---

In AccessBuddy, `fobRequests.paidAt` is set only by the `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook, so a late or failed webhook leaves a paid request looking unpaid. The money-owed states are SUBMITTED and AWAITING_PAYMENT; priced member requests rest in SUBMITTED until the member pays or asks for an exemption (the client payment step makes no API call).

**Why:** PR #104 (merged 14 Oct 2026) added Require Payment, Resend Payment Link, a nightly abandoned-payment sweep and a signed cancel link. Both the advisor and the code-review agent independently flagged that keying any of those off `paidAt` could email "please pay" to someone who had paid, or cancel a paid request with no refund.

**How to apply:** before any new action that demands, resends, forgives or cancels payment, call `retrievePaymentIntent` (apps/web/src/lib/stripe.ts) and branch on `succeeded` / `processing`; `ensurePaymentIntent` and `requestHasPaymentInFlight` in `lib/services/requests.ts` already do this and should be reused. A cancelled intent (cancel then reopen) or a price change needs a fresh intent, and the old one should be voided. The cancel link token is HMAC over `cancel:v1:tenantId:requestId:expiry` with `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`; rotating that secret invalidates outstanding cancel links. See [[gotcha-accessbuddy-prod-access]] for how PRs are opened and merged from the Mac.

---
name: gotcha-accessbuddy-paidat-is-a-cache
description: AccessBuddy fobRequests.paidAt lags Stripe; any action that demands or forgives money must read the PaymentIntent from Stripe first
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 145cf10e-206a-4ef3-926b-5bbd8d94112d
  modified: 2026-10-14T10:13:15.259Z
---

In AccessBuddy, `fobRequests.paidAt` is set only by the `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook, so a late or failed webhook leaves a paid request looking unpaid. The money-owed states are SUBMITTED and AWAITING_PAYMENT; priced member requests rest in SUBMITTED until the member pays or asks for an exemption (the client payment step makes no API call).

**Why:** PR #104 (merged 14 Oct 2026) added Require Payment, Resend Payment Link, a nightly abandoned-payment sweep and a signed cancel link. Both the advisor and the code-review agent independently flagged that keying any of those off `paidAt` could email "please pay" to someone who had paid, or cancel a paid request with no refund.

**How to apply:** before any new action that demands, resends, forgives or cancels payment, call `retrievePaymentIntent` (apps/web/src/lib/stripe.ts) and branch on `succeeded` / `processing`; `ensurePaymentIntent` and `requestHasPaymentInFlight` in `lib/services/requests.ts` already do this and should be reused. A cancelled intent (cancel then reopen) or a price change needs a fresh intent, and the old one should be voided. The cancel link token is HMAC over `cancel:v1:tenantId:requestId:expiry` with `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET`; rotating that secret invalidates outstanding cancel links. See [[gotcha-accessbuddy-prod-access]] for how PRs are opened and merged from the Mac.
